root_cause.text: In btrfs_create_new_inode(), the code does not pre-check whether the parent directory's dir item has enough space to accommodate a new entry when hash collisions cause entries to be packed into the same dir item, so an insertion failure later forces a transaction abort instead of returning a graceful error.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early call to `btrfs_check_dir_item_collision()` in `btrfs_create_new_inode()` before any tree updates, with the explicit comment: "check if we can add the name to the parent directory. We want to avoid a dir item overflow in case we have an existing dir item due to existing name hash collisions." The CVE description confirms that reaching the leaf size limit triggers a transaction abort.
